claims.text: James Watson and Francis Crick published their double-helix model of DNA in 1953.
Banting and Best worked on insulin, Darwin and Wallace on evolution by natural selection, and Hahn and Strassmann on nuclear fission; none of these pairs proposed the double helix.
Watson and Crick's model drew on X-ray diffraction images from Rosalind Franklin's lab at King's College London, including Photo 51.
Watson, Crick and Maurice Wilkins shared the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
